question: what it costs to run the MPC over the same field the commitments use

superseded_measurement.why_it_was_wrong: The circuit was compiled with `-P <prime>`. MP-SPDZ prints, in the compile output, `WARNING: --prime/-P activates code that usually isn't the most efficient variant. Consider using --field/-F and set the prime only during the actual computation.` That warning was in the output of every run and was not read. Compiling with `-F <bits>` and passing the prime to the virtual machine at run time is the supported path, and it removes the whole penalty.
superseded_measurement.kept_because: a measurement that was published to three repositories and a slide deck, and was wrong by seven times on the figure everything else was reasoned from

result.note: Rounds unchanged. Traffic exactly 2.00x, which is the element width going from 16 bytes to 32 and nothing else. Wall clock 1.07x at 15 ms and 1.06x at 120 ms --- cheaper cross-region, because the round count does not move and the round trip is what dominates there. Every arm verified against the cleartext answer.
result.consequence: Matching the field is affordable, so threshold_sigma assembles and the quote proof is publicly verifiable for six to eight per cent. The input check is no longer the cheap alternative to that --- it is a fast pre-check that still costs one round on top, and catches a substituted input immediately rather than when the proof fails.
